BAYLOR ATHLETICS
Software and Technology Management Framework
Status | Draft for discussion
Date | August 14, 2026
Prepared by | Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics
Responsible offices | Intercollegiate Athletics; Information Technology Services; Office of General Counsel; University Compliance and Risk Services
Review and approval | Business Office and ITS serve as the two control points. Final policy language should be reviewed by the Office of General Counsel, University Compliance and Risk Services, ITS, and Privacy.
1. Purpose
To increase the efficiency and timeliness of requests for software and technology purchase and implementation, and to establish a consistent, transparent process for how those decisions are made, reviewed, and renewed.
1.1  Policy statement
Baylor Athletics shall select, acquire, implement, use, access, disclose, retain, and dispose of software, technology, and the data they generate only for authorized athletics, sports medicine, health, safety, performance, compliance, and operational purposes, and only in accordance with Baylor University policies, applicable law, NCAA guidance, contractual obligations, and approved data-governance practices.
Software and technology must be governed through a written plan, routine education, defined data rights, structured technology review, and continuous improvement.
1.2  Reason for the framework
Technology used in athletics may collect biometric, health-related, performance, workload, recovery, video, sensor, survey, software, mobile-application, and other individual-level data. Responsible use of these technologies requires coordination across Athletics, Sports Medicine, Information Technology Services, Privacy, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, and Records Management.
This framework is intended to help Baylor Athletics support student-athlete health, safety, privacy, autonomy, data security, and performance while reducing legal, regulatory, contractual, operational, and reputational risk.
The framework started with athlete performance technology, which handles the most sensitive data and is subject to the clearest NCAA guidance. It is written to serve as the department's general approach to all technology. The process below applies to every technology request in the department, and the depth of review depends on the request's scope.
2. Scope and terminology
2.1  Scope
Technology refers to tangible items like devices, wearables, equipment, and applications. Software refers to the platforms and systems those items connect to. The two are rarely purchased independently, and this framework covers both.
The framework is not limited to performance, health, and wellness. Athlete performance technology sits inside that scope and triggers a review. A request that does not involve any athlete data still goes through the same review mechanism.
2.2  Individuals and entities affected
Baylor Athletics staff, coaches, sports medicine personnel, strength and conditioning staff, analysts, administrators, student support staff, and other Baylor personnel who select, use, access, interpret, or disclose technology and the data it generates.
Student-athletes whose data is collected, used, analyzed, inferred, stored, or disclosed through these technologies.
Vendors, contractors, consultants, and other third parties that collect, store, process, analyze, host, transmit, or receive Baylor Athletics data on Baylor's behalf.
Baylor units supporting Athletics, including ITS, Information Security, Office of General Counsel, University Compliance and Risk Services, Privacy, Internal Audit, Procurement, and records-management functions.
2.3  Exclusions
This framework does not replace or supersede Baylor policies that already govern specific categories of data, systems, conduct, records, or legal obligations. Where a more specific Baylor policy applies, that policy continues to govern. This document should be read as an Athletics-specific overlay that routes technology decisions into existing Baylor governance channels rather than around them.
2.4  Definitions
Term | Definition for this framework
Technology | Tangible items such as devices, wearables, sensors, cameras, and equipment, together with the applications that operate them.
Software | The platforms and systems that technology connects to, including hosted, cloud, and on-premises applications.
Athlete Performance Technology | Any device, sensor, wearable, software, mobile application, camera, survey, analytics platform, AI-enabled system, or other technology used to collect, infer, monitor, analyze, store, or communicate biometric, performance, workload, recovery, wellness, health, safety, training, competition, or related data about student-athletes.
Athlete Performance Technology Data | Data collected, generated, inferred, stored, analyzed, or disclosed through athlete performance technologies, including performance metrics, physiological metrics, sleep, hydration, nutrition, stress indicators, recovery, training load, practice or game analytics, and related data.
Restricted / Protected Data | Data subject to Baylor data-classification requirements and heightened safeguards, including where applicable PHI, FERPA records, biometric identifiers, credentials, SSNs, financial information, IRB-related research data, and other regulated or sensitive data.
Medical Decision-Making Data | Data used, intended to be used, or reasonably likely to be used to inform medical management, injury evaluation, treatment, rehabilitation, or return-to-play decisions.
Approved Use Case | A documented and approved purpose, user population, data category, vendor or system, and data lifecycle for a technology.
Student-Athlete Notice | A plain-language explanation to student-athletes of what data is collected, why, who may access it, permissible uses, retention, rights, questions, and concerns.
3. Alignment with NCAA guidance
The NCAA Sports Science Institute has published guidance on the Responsible Use of Performance Technologies in College Athletics. That guidance sets the expectations each institution is to meet and leaves the method of implementation to the institution, according to its own structure and resources. This framework is Baylor Athletics' implementation. Appendix A maps each NCAA recommendation to the section of this framework that carries it.
4. Intended outcomes
A consistent, shared understanding of the entire inventory of software and technology in use across the department.
Improved utilization of what the department already owns.
Coordinated renewal and term review, giving the department advance visibility of contract end dates and the lead time to evaluate options well before a renewal decision is due.
Increased staff fluency so that sport administrators and unit staff can address technology questions with confidence.
5. Roles and responsibilities
The roles below combine the operating roles that move a request through the process with the review functions that must be applied before a request can clear.
Role | Responsibility in this framework
Head Coach, Admin, and/or Unit Director | Initiates the request. Completes the Idea Form and internal ATH Form, including the declared data category and proposed review level.
Athletics Executive Sponsor | Owns Athletics operational compliance with this framework and ensures teams, coaches, and staff use approved technologies and approved use cases.
Business Office | First control point.  Filters  all requests before they proceed. Budget, contract, and duplication check process through the Business Office.
ITS / Information Security | Second control point. Technical, security, and integration review; confirms the system can be supported. Reviews access, authentication, storage, transmission, monitoring, incident response, and security controls. These requests carry integration, contract, and security implications across departments, so ITS is represented at a supervisory level with the authority to commit ITS resources and to decide on integration and security posture. Technical staff are brought in for specialist review as the request requires.
Director of Applied Performance | Single point of contact and facilitator. Holds the weekly standing meeting with ITS and relays status to project managers and stakeholders. Facilitator, not owner; not the subject-matter expert and not the project manager.
Assigned Project Manager | Owns delivery of the individual project. May be administrative staff other than the Director of Applied Performance.
Sport Administrator | Signs off on renewal decisions at Phase 3, informed by the usage review.
Health & Wellness / Sports Medicine | Reviews requests involving physiologic or health data. Must be involved where data may inform medical decision-making, injury evaluation, rehabilitation, or return-to-play decisions.
Athletics Compliance | Coordinates NCAA, conference, student-athlete, and departmental compliance implications.
Office of General Counsel / Privacy | Reviews FERPA, HIPAA, Texas privacy, consent, data rights, disclosure, vendor terms, and legal holds.
Procurement / Contracting | Ensures vendor contracts address ownership, permitted use, storage, access, data sharing, AI training, automated decision-making, downstream sharing, retention, deletion, portability, and breach notification.
Coaches, Staff, and Users | Use technology only for approved purposes, complete required training, avoid unauthorized disclosure, and report suspected misuse or incidents.
Student-Athlete Representatives | Provide feedback on transparency, education, perceived benefits, and potential unintended impacts of technology use.
6. Levels of review
The level of review depends on three things: what data the technology touches, how many units it serves, and what the department is committing to in cost and contract term.
Level | Applies when | Review includes
Level 1 Standard Review | No athlete data; single unit; low or one-time cost | Compliance, Privacy, Ownership, Transparency, Interoperability
Level 2 Enhanced Review | Performance data, multi-team use, or recurring cost | Full review
Level 3 Comprehensive Review | Physiologic or health data; external data sharing; third-party processing of athlete data | Full review, plus data protection review and Health & Wellness / medical sign-off
The level is proposed by the requester at intake and confirmed at the control points.
7. Exceptions
7.1  Urgent and “emergency” requests
Urgent requests clear the same control points, with a short risk checklist completed at intake to surface issues that would otherwise delay the request: data category, contract term, integration dependency, and whether athlete data leaves Baylor.
A request directed by an administrative lead enters the expedited lane on receipt. This provides documentation for what qualifies as urgent, so the distinction does not have to be determined on a case-by-case basis at intake. An expedited request still clears both control points and still carries the review level its data and commitment call for.
8. The three phases
Phase 1 — Proposal, Approval, Purchase
1.1  A request is initiated by the Director of Applied Performance, a Head Coach, or any Admin Unit Director.
1.2  The requester completes the Technology Idea Form and the internal ATH Form. The request must declare its data category and proposed review level.
1.3  The request goes to the Business Office. The Business Office serves as the filter for all requests and the first control point.
1.4  The forms are submitted to ITS for technical, security, and integration review. This is the second control point. The Athletics steps described in this framework feed that review; they do not create a separate ITS workflow.
1.5  The request is evaluated against the Technology Evaluation Scorecard.
1.6  A request is disseminated for purchase only after clearing both control points. Declined requests are returned with documented reasons.
1.7  The Director of Applied Performance holds a weekly standing meeting with the ITS representative to review the status of all open requests across all units. The requester may be brought into the meeting where input is needed; their standing attendance is not expected. The Director of Applied Performance provides regular updates on the status of any open request.
Phase 2 — Implementation and Product Use
2.1  A project manager is assigned. This may be administrative staff other than the Director of Applied, depending on the unit and the system.
2.2  Status flows from the weekly ITS standing meeting through the Director of Applied to the assigned project manager and stakeholders, so that every open request has a known owner.
2.3  Open requests are tracked as follows: project, item, requester, project manager, date submitted, desired implementation date, current status, and what is holding it up.
Phase 3 — Product Review and Renewal Decision
3.1  Review is triggered at six months, or at the end of the competitive season, whichever is longer. Tools used primarily in season are therefore judged on in-season usage.
3.2  The review compares actual utilization against the intent stated on the original request.
3.3  Low utilization opens a diagnostic conversation before a renewal conclusion.
3.4  The outcome is renew, modify or renegotiate, or discontinue.
9. Workflow
Appendix A — NCAA Performance Technologies Recommendations Crosswalk
The NCAA Sport Science Institute's consensus guidance on the responsible use of performance technologies in college athletics is organized around five recommendations. The table below carries each recommendation, the NCAA strategy, the corresponding Baylor action step, and the section of this framework where it is addressed. Entries marked “planned for Version 1” identify work that is scoped and scheduled for the next revision of this document.
Recommendation | NCAA Strategy | Baylor Action Step | Framework Reference
1. Policy | Create a written plan. Build it with a multidisciplinary team (student-athletes, sports medicine, coaches, admin, legal, IT). Review it regularly. | Form a MDT (Multi-disciplinary Team) or a Performance Technology Working Group, draft the plan, and present it to S-A Services Staff for input. | §1.1  Policy statement — the written-plan requirement §1.2  Reason for the framework §5  Roles and responsibilities — review functions spanning sports medicine, compliance, legal, ITS, procurement, and Student-Athlete Representatives §8  Phase 1.7 — standing review cadence with ITS Standing Performance Technology Working Group and the framework’s own review cycle: planned for Version 1.
2. Education | Train everyone at least once a year. Tailor content by audience. Cover limitations, data privacy, informed consent, and departmental policies. | Add a performance technology module to existing compliance sessions and new student-athletes’ onboarding. Different content for coaches, Athletic Medicine, Athletics Performance, and student-athletes, etc. | §1.1  Policy statement — routine education as a governing requirement §5  Coaches, Staff, and Users — required training §5  Student-Athlete Representatives — feedback on education A dedicated Education and Training section, carrying annual cadence and audience-specific content: planned for Version 1.
3. Data Management | Establish who owns the data, where it lives, who can see it, and what it can be used for. Plan for transfer student-athletes. | Run a full technology inventory across all sports. Work with legal and IT to establish ownership, access, and transfer protocols. Develop a data rights/release consent template. | §1.1  Policy statement — authorized purposes; access, retention, and disposal §2.4  Definitions — Restricted / Protected Data; Medical Decision-Making Data; Approved Use Case; Student-Athlete Notice §4  Intended outcomes — department-wide technology inventory §5  ITS / Information Security — access, authentication, storage, transmission §5  Office of General Counsel / Privacy — consent, data rights, disclosure §5  Procurement / Contracting — ownership, permitted use, retention, deletion, portability §6  Level 3 Comprehensive Review — external data sharing; third-party processing Transfer student-athlete data protocol and the data rights / release consent template: planned for Version 1.
4. Tech Selection | Evaluate quality (accuracy, reliability, validity) before you buy. Use evidence-based frameworks. Decisions should be made by a cross-functional group. | Build a Technology Evaluation Checklist. Route all new purchases through the Working Group (MDT). Establish a scalable review process with documentation. | §5  Roles and responsibilities — cross-functional review functions §6  Levels of review — Level 1 Standard, Level 2 Enhanced, Level 3 Comprehensive §7  Exceptions — expedited requests clear the same control points §8  Phase 1.2–1.6 — Technology Idea Form and internal ATH Form; Business Office control point; ITS control point; Technology Evaluation Scorecard at 1.5; documented decision Quality criteria (accuracy, reliability, validity) are carried in the Technology Evaluation Scorecard, maintained as a companion artifact to this framework.
5. Continuous Improvement | Collect feedback from student-athletes, coaches, and staff on a regular basis. Student-athlete feedback is not optional. Use it to update the plan. | Annual student-athlete survey. The Working Group runs an annual review. Each technology gets a continuation, modification, or discontinuation decision. | §8  Phase 3.1–3.4 — review at six months or end of competitive season; utilization measured against stated intent; diagnostic conversation; outcome of renew, modify or renegotiate, or discontinue §5  Student-Athlete Representatives — feedback on transparency, education, perceived benefits, and potential unintended impacts Annual student-athlete survey and the annual Working Group review of the framework: planned for Version 1.
A.1  Foundational concepts
Two foundational concepts in the NCAA guidance sit alongside the five recommendations. The breadth of the NCAA definition of performance technology, which reaches cameras, surveys, and applications and not only wearables, is carried in the §2.1 scope statement and the §2.4 definition of Athlete Performance Technology. Student-athlete rights, informed consent, and the potential for unintended impacts, including effects on mental health and body image, are reflected in the §2.4 Student-Athlete Notice, the §5 Office of General Counsel / Privacy and Health & Wellness / Sports Medicine review functions, and the §5 Student-Athlete Representatives feedback role. Explicit treatment of unintended impacts within the education content and the annual student-athlete survey is planned for Version 1.
A.2  Relationship to institutional workflow
This framework is an Athletics-side overlay, as stated in §2.3. It routes technology decisions into the existing Baylor governance channels rather than around them. The Athletics intake and control points described in §8 are intended to complement institutional review rather than to operate as a separate workflow.=====
BAYLOR ATHLETICS  ·  APPLIED PERFORMANCE
Technology Evaluation Scorecard
Adapted from the Sports Tech Research Network Quality Framework for Sports Technologies, and from the existing Baylor Applied Performance assessment sheet.
Status | DRAFT v0.9 — for discussion, 2026-08-10

How to use this scorecard
The scorecard has two parts that work differently.
Gate features are pass or fail. A fail on any gate feature stops the request regardless of how the rest of the scorecard reads. These are the features that create institutional risk or long-term lock-in, and they cannot be offset by strength elsewhere.
Scored features are rated Strong, Adequate or Weak. They inform the decision and the negotiation; they do not by themselves stop it. Use N/A where a feature genuinely does not apply, and say why in the note column.
Rating language follows the STRN convention: Strong — excellent, with no useful further improvement possible or only minor opportunity; Adequate — acceptable, with clear opportunities for improvement; Weak — a weakness needing improvement.
A fail is not necessarily the end A gate failure means the request cannot proceed as submitted. It is often the start of a conversation with the vendor — unclear data ownership terms and absent export capability are frequently negotiable, and asking for them is easiest before signature.
Part 1  ·  Gate features — pass / fail
Feature | Definition | Pass | Fail | Evidence / note
Compliance | The extent to which the technology is aligned with relevant laws and regulation. | ☐ | ☐ | 
Privacy | The extent to which the confidentiality of, and access to, information about the user is protected. | ☐ | ☐ | 
Ownership | The ability to access, create, modify, package, derive benefit from, sell or remove outputs, and to assign those privileges, is clearly defined. | ☐ | ☐ | 
Transparency | Recalls, feature updates, and honest, timely reporting to users and governing bodies. Security vulnerabilities are logged, disclosed and resolved. | ☐ | ☐ | 
Interoperability | Ability to connect to and communicate with other systems at foundational, structural or semantic levels. | ☐ | ☐ | 
Any fail above halts the request. Record the reason and, where relevant, what the vendor would need to change.
Part 2  ·  Evidence quality — does it measure what it claims?
Feature | Definition | Str | Adq | Wk | N/A | Evidence / note
Accuracy | Agreement of the technology's output with a current gold standard for similar measurement. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | 
Repeatability | Output remains the same under similar test conditions over a short period. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | 
Reproducibility | Output remains the same under changed conditions — different users, devices, locations, or extended time. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | 
Specifications | Capacity, sample rate and dimensions are clearly available to the user. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | 
Construct validity | Measures the specific area of interest, and differentiates between groups or conditions. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | 
Concurrent validity | Output relates to a previously validated measure administered at the same time. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | 
Predictive validity | Output has been shown to predict a future state or outcome. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | 
Functionality | Provides functions that meet stated and implied needs, with limitations clearly stated. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ |

Feature | Definition | Str | Adq | Wk | N/A | Evidence / note

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

"""Appendix forms A-E for the Performance Technology Best Practices guide.

Imported by build_guide.py; each function returns a finished BaylorDoc.
Keep form content here and guide content in build_guide.py.
"""
from baylor_docstyle import BaylorDoc

STATUS = "Draft v1 for discussion"
BOX = "☐"


def _head(title, deck, use):
    d = BaylorDoc(title, deck=deck, status=STATUS)
    d.meta([
        ["Part of", "Performance Technology Best Practices (Baylor Athletics), Draft v1"],
        ["Used by", use],
        ["Owner", "Performance Technology Working Group"],
        ["Version", "Draft v1, October 2026. Pending review as marked."],
    ])
    return d


def consent_form():
    d = _head("Appendix A: Student-Athlete Performance Technology Consent",
              "What Baylor Athletics collects with performance technology, why, who sees it, "
              "and what you can say yes or no to.",
              "Every student-athlete, at the start of each academic year and whenever a new "
              "technology is introduced in their sport. Kept by Athletic Medicine.")
    d.callout("Read this first",
              "Some data is collected from every athlete in a team setting and cannot be "
              "switched off, such as venue tracking and video of practice. You are told about "
              "it here (Part 2). Other data needs your yes before it is collected (Part 3). "
              "Saying no to anything in Part 3 has **no effect on your scholarship, playing "
              "time or place on the team.** [Pending OGC: final consent and notice language.]")

    d.section("Who you are")
    d.table(["Field", "Entry"], [
        ["Name", ""], ["Sport", ""], ["Academic year", ""],
        ["This form is", f"{BOX} Annual consent    {BOX} New technology added    {BOX} Change of consent"],
    ], widths=[1.8, 4.9])

    d.section("Notice: data collected in team settings")
    d.para("These are part of normal team activity. You can ask to see your own data at any time.")
    d.table(["Technology (examples)", "What it records", "Who sees it"], [
        ["Video of practice and competition", "Movement, technique, tactics", "Coaches, Athletic Performance, Applied Performance, Athletic Medicine"],
        ["Team GPS or venue tracking (e.g. Catapult, Kinexon)", "Distance, speed, accelerations, training load", "Athletic Performance and Applied Performance; coaches see summaries"],
        ["Force plate and jump testing (e.g. VALD ForceDecks)", "Jump height, force, asymmetry, readiness", "Athletic Performance and Applied Performance; Athletic Medicine for injury and return to play"],
        ["Wellness check-ins", "Sleep, soreness, stress", "Athletic Medicine and Athletic Performance; coaches see flags only"],
    ], widths=[2.2, 2.0, 2.5])
    d.note("The list for your sport is attached by your sport's Athletic Performance coach. "
           "[Pending OGC: whether team GPS and testing sit under notice or consent.]")

    d.section("Consent: data that needs your yes")
    d.table(["Item", "Yes", "No"], [
        ["Wearables worn outside team sessions (heart rate, HRV, sleep rings or straps)", BOX, BOX],
        ["Body composition testing (DEXA or similar)", BOX, BOX],
        ["Cognitive testing (e.g. S2 Cognition)", BOX, BOX],
        ["Use of my de-identified data by a vendor to build norms or improve products", BOX, BOX],
        ["Use of my de-identified data in research (only with IRB approval)", BOX, BOX],
        ["Sharing my individual data with anyone outside Baylor Athletics (for example a new school, a pro team, an agent or an NIL partner). Each release still needs a separate written request from me.", BOX, BOX],
    ], widths=[5.3, 0.7, 0.7])

    d.section("Your rights")
    d.bullets([
        "You can see your own data, and ask for a copy, at any time.",
        "You can withdraw consent for anything in Part 3 at any time by telling Athletic "
        "Medicine or the Data Steward in writing. Collection stops from that date.",
        "Your data is not sent to another school or anyone outside Baylor without your "
        "written request.",
        "Data is kept for the retention period Baylor sets, then deleted. "
        "[Pending OGC: retention period.] You may ask for earlier deletion when you leave, "
        "where the law allows.",
        "Coaches do not see medical data. Athletic Medicine alone decides return to play.",
        "If something about your data feels wrong, or the numbers are stressing you out, "
        "tell Athletic Medicine, the Data Steward or a SAAC representative.",
    ])

    d.section("Signatures")
    d.table(["", "Signature", "Date"], [
        ["Student-athlete", "", ""],
        ["Parent or guardian (under 18 only)", "", ""],
        ["Witness (Athletic Medicine)", "", ""],
    ], widths=[2.3, 3.0, 1.4])
    d.note("Contact: the Data Steward, Applied Performance. Record kept with the "
           "student-athlete's Athletic Medicine file. [Pending Athletic Medicine: system of record.]")
    return d


def vendor_checklist():
    d = _head("Appendix B: Vendor Data Addendum and Contract Checklist",
              "The terms every contract must cover before a vendor holds Baylor athlete data.",
              "Procurement and the requester, at purchase and at renewal. The Working Group "
              "uses it for the contract audit.")
    d.table(["Field", "Entry"], [
        ["Vendor and product", ""], ["Contract or order number", ""],
        ["Renewal or end date", ""], ["Data category", f"{BOX} Performance   {BOX} Physiologic or health   {BOX} Cognitive   {BOX} Body composition   {BOX} None"],
        ["Reviewed by / date", ""],
    ], widths=[1.8, 4.9])

    d.section("Required terms")
    d.para("Mark each term Met, Not met, or N/A. Any **Not met** in rows 1 to 6 sends the "
           "contract back to the vendor before signature or renewal.")
    rows = [
        ["1", "Ownership", "Baylor owns the data. The vendor has no rights beyond delivering the service. [Pending Chris/OGC: ownership position.]"],
        ["2", "Permitted use", "Data is used only to provide the service to Baylor. No sale, rental or licensing."],
        ["3", "Exit: return and deletion", "When the contract ends or the product is dropped, the vendor returns all data in a standard format within 30 days, then deletes it and certifies deletion in writing."],
        ["4", "Breach notification", "The vendor tells Baylor of a suspected breach within 72 hours. [Pending ITS/OGC: notice window.]"],
        ["5", "AI and model training", "No use of Baylor data, identified or de-identified, to train or tune AI models without written opt-in from Baylor."],
        ["6", "Data for discount / norm pooling", "No price discount tied to sharing data. Any pooling of de-identified data into vendor norms is listed in the contract, opt-in, and disclosed to athletes."],
        ["7", "Storage and jurisdiction", "Where data is stored and in which country. Encryption in transit and at rest."],
        ["8", "Downstream sharing", "Named sub-processors only. No sharing with third parties (including leagues, scouts, media) without Baylor's written consent."],
        ["9", "Access and accounts", "The admin account is owned by a Baylor institutional address, not a personal one. Baylor can add and remove users itself."],
        ["10", "Retention", "Vendor keeps data no longer than Baylor's retention period."],
        ["11", "Portability", "Full export available at any time in a documented, non-proprietary format (CSV or similar)."],
        ["12", "Algorithm transparency", "The vendor documents how derived scores are calculated and tells Baylor before changing them."],
        ["13", "Athlete access", "Baylor can give an athlete a copy of their own data on request."],
        ["14", "Audit", "Baylor may request the vendor's security attestation (e.g. SOC 2) each year."],
    ]
    d.table(["#", "Term", "What the contract must say", "Met / Not met / N/A"],
            [r + [""] for r in rows], widths=[0.3, 1.4, 3.8, 1.2])

    d.section("Decision")
    d.table(["Outcome", "Mark"], [
        ["Sign or renew as written", BOX], ["Sign or renew after the listed changes", BOX],
        ["Do not sign or renew", BOX],
    ], widths=[5.5, 1.2])
    d.note("A standard data addendum built from rows 1 to 14 goes to OGC and Procurement "
           "for approval. [Pending OGC/Procurement: approved addendum wording.]")
    return d


def offboarding_checklist():
    d = _head("Appendix C: Staff Offboarding and Platform Handover Checklist",
              "What happens to accounts, data and know-how when a staff member who runs or "
              "uses performance technology leaves or changes role.",
              "The departing person's supervisor, with the Data Steward and ITS. Start on "
              "notice of departure; finish by the last working day.")
    d.table(["Field", "Entry"], [
        ["Departing staff member / role", ""], ["Last working day", ""],
        ["Supervisor", ""], ["Data Steward", ""],
    ], widths=[2.2, 4.5])

    d.section("Platforms this person ran or used")
    d.para("One row per platform. Take the list from the technology inventory and add "
           "anything missing.")
    d.table(["Platform", "Admin or user?", "Institutional admin confirmed", "Access removed (date)", "Custodian after departure"],
            [["", "", BOX, "", ""] for _ in range(6)],
            widths=[1.6, 1.1, 1.3, 1.3, 1.4])

    d.section("Before the last day")
    d.bullets([
        f"{BOX} Every platform's admin account is a Baylor institutional account, not the person's own email. Ownership moved where it was not.",
        f"{BOX} A named custodian and a backup are set for each platform (Section 6 of the guide).",
        f"{BOX} Exports, scripts, report templates and pipelines the person built are in a Baylor-owned location (department drive or repository), not a personal drive or laptop.",
        f"{BOX} A handover note is written for each system they ran: what it does, how data gets in, how reports are built and sent, who receives them, where credentials and API keys are held, known problems.",
        f"{BOX} Vendor contacts, renewal dates and licence counts are updated in the technology inventory.",
        f"{BOX} Any athlete data held locally (laptop, phone, USB, personal cloud) is returned or deleted, and the person confirms it in writing.",
        f"{BOX} Scheduled jobs or automations running under the person's account are moved to a service or institutional account.",
    ])

    d.section("On or after the last day")
    d.bullets([
        f"{BOX} Access removed on every platform on the last working day, and ITS has disabled single sign-on.",
        f"{BOX} API keys and shared passwords the person knew are rotated.",
        f"{BOX} Vendors are told of the change of contact.",
        f"{BOX} The custodian has logged in and run one normal report end to end.",
    ])

    d.section("Sign-off")
    d.table(["Role", "Name", "Signature", "Date"], [
        ["Departing staff member", "", "", ""], ["Supervisor", "", "", ""],
        ["Data Steward", "", "", ""], ["ITS", "", "", ""],
    ], widths=[1.8, 1.7, 2.0, 1.2])
    d.note("[Pending ITS: the access-removal timeline and who disables single sign-on.]")
    return d


def annual_review_checklist():
    d = _head("Appendix D: Annual Review Checklist",
              "The once-a-year review of the guide, every technology in use, education and feedback.",
              "The Performance Technology Working Group, each spring, after the student-athlete "
              "and staff surveys close.")
    d.table(["Field", "Entry"], [["Review year", ""], ["Meeting date", ""], ["Chair", ""]],
            widths=[1.8, 4.9])

    d.section("Inputs gathered before the meeting")
    d.bullets([
        f"{BOX} Student-athlete survey results (SSI Rec 5.2) and SAAC feedback.",
        f"{BOX} Staff survey results (SSI Rec 5.3).",
        f"{BOX} Updated technology inventory: products, units, data category, renewal dates.",
        f"{BOX} Utilization review for each technology up for renewal (framework Phase 3).",
        f"{BOX} Education attendance by group (SSI Rec 2.1).",
        f"{BOX} Consent records: coverage by sport, withdrawals, opt-out rates.",
        f"{BOX} Concerns raised, data releases made, and any incidents during the year.",
        f"{BOX} Contract audit progress against the priority list.",
    ])

    d.section("Technology-by-technology review")
    d.table(["Technology", "Question it answers", "Still used as intended?", "Harms reported?", "Decision"],
            [["", "", "", "", "Continue / Modify / Stop"] for _ in range(5)],
            widths=[1.3, 1.6, 1.2, 1.1, 1.5])
    d.note("If the data is not being acted on, the default decision is Stop: "
           "collect only what we use.")

    d.section("Guide review")
    d.bullets([
        f"{BOX} Each section of the guide read and checked against current practice.",
        f"{BOX} New NCAA, conference or legal guidance checked.",
        f"{BOX} Pending items from last year closed or carried forward with an owner.",
        f"{BOX} Changes agreed, version number raised, revision log updated.",
        f"{BOX} Summary of findings and changes shared with student-athletes through SAAC.",
        f"{BOX} One-page annual report sent to the document owner.",
    ])
    d.section("Sign-off")
    d.table(["Role", "Name", "Signature", "Date"],
            [["Working Group chair", "", "", ""], ["Document owner", "", "", ""]],
            widths=[1.8, 1.7, 2.0, 1.2])
    return d


def intake_form():
    d = _head("Appendix E: Technology Intake and Evaluation Form",
              "Start from the question. One form and one scoring sheet for every new "
              "performance technology, trial or renewal.",
              "The requester completes Part 1. Reviewers complete Parts 2 to 4 before the "
              "framework's Business Office and ITS control points.")
    d.callout("How this fits the framework",
              "This form replaces both the March 2026 evaluation checklist and the August "
              "2026 Technology Evaluation Scorecard. It is the scoring instrument at Phase 1.5 "
              "of the Software and Technology Management Framework. Gates are pass or fail; "
              "everything else is rated Strong, Adequate or Weak.")

    d.section("The question (requester)")
    d.table(["Prompt", "Answer"], [
        ["What decision or question will this technology answer?", ""],
        ["Who will act on the answer, and how often?", ""],
        ["What do we use to answer it today, and why is that not enough?", ""],
        ["Product, vendor, sport(s) and number of athletes", ""],
        ["Data it collects (tick all)", f"{BOX} Performance   {BOX} Physiologic or health   {BOX} Cognitive   {BOX} Body composition   {BOX} Video   {BOX} None"],
        ["Does athlete data leave Baylor (vendor cloud, norm pooling)?", f"{BOX} Yes   {BOX} No"],
        ["Proposed review level (framework §6)", f"{BOX} Level 1   {BOX} Level 2   {BOX} Level 3"],
        ["Total cost and contract term", ""],
        ["Who will run it day to day, and who is the backup?", ""],
    ], widths=[3.0, 3.7])

    d.section("Gates: pass or fail")
    d.para("A fail on any gate stops the request as submitted. It often starts a negotiation "
           "with the vendor rather than ending the request.")
    d.table(["Gate", "Pass if", "Pass", "Fail"], [
        ["Fit to the question", "Part 1 names a decision someone will act on.", BOX, BOX],
        ["Compliance and privacy", "Meets Baylor data policy, FERPA and HIPAA where they apply; data encrypted; access by role.", BOX, BOX],
        ["Ownership and exit", "Contract can meet Appendix B rows 1 to 6, including return and deletion at exit.", BOX, BOX],
        ["Student-athlete impact", "No foreseeable harm to well-being, body image or mental health that cannot be managed.", BOX, BOX],
        ["Transparency", "Vendor explains how derived scores are calculated and discloses changes.", BOX, BOX],
        ["Interoperability", "Data can be exported in a standard format.", BOX, BOX],
    ], widths=[1.6, 3.7, 0.7, 0.7])

    d.section("Rated features")
    d.table(["Feature", "Question", "Strong", "Adequate", "Weak", "N/A"], [
        ["Accuracy", "Agrees with a gold-standard measure?", BOX, BOX, BOX, BOX],
        ["Reliability", "Same result on repeat tests, devices and users?", BOX, BOX, BOX, BOX],
        ["Validity", "Measures what matters; independent (not vendor-funded) evidence?", BOX, BOX, BOX, BOX],
        ["Usability", "Staff and athletes can use it without heavy training?", BOX, BOX, BOX, BOX],
        ["Robustness and support", "Works in our conditions; responsive vendor support?", BOX, BOX, BOX, BOX],
        ["Integration", "Fits our existing systems and reporting?", BOX, BOX, BOX, BOX],
        ["Value", "Cost justified against the question in Part 1?", BOX, BOX, BOX, BOX],
        ["Peer check", "At least two comparable programs consulted?", BOX, BOX, BOX, BOX],
    ], widths=[1.4, 2.9, 0.6, 0.7, 0.55, 0.55])

    d.section("Decision rule and recommendation")
    d.bullets([
        "**Proceed:** all gates pass, and no Weak on Accuracy, Reliability or Validity.",
        "**Trial (30 to 60 days, hard end date):** all gates pass, but the evidence is "
        "Weak or untested in our setting. Report back at 90 days.",
        "**Decline or renegotiate:** any gate fails.",
    ])
    d.table(["Recommendation", "Mark"], [
        ["Approve", BOX], ["Approve as trial with end date ____", BOX],
        ["Approve subject to contract changes", BOX], ["Decline", BOX],
    ], widths=[5.5, 1.2])
    d.table(["Reviewer", "Name", "Date"], [
        ["Applied Performance", "", ""], ["Athletic Medicine (Level 3)", "", ""],
        ["ITS", "", ""], ["Business Office", "", ""],
    ], widths=[2.4, 2.8, 1.5])
    return d


FORMS = [
    ("A_Consent", consent_form),
    ("B_VendorChecklist", vendor_checklist),
    ("C_OffboardingChecklist", offboarding_checklist),
    ("D_AnnualReview", annual_review_checklist),
    ("E_TechIntake", intake_form),
]

## remarkable
# reMarkable MCP Server

Access documents from your reMarkable tablet. All operations are read-only.

## Available Tools

- `remarkable_browse(path, query)` - Browse folders or search for documents
- `remarkable_read(document, content_type, page, grep)` - Read document content with pagination
- `remarkable_recent(limit)` - Get recently modified documents
- `remarkable_status()` - Check connection and diagnose issues
- `remarkable_image(document, page, include_ocr)` - Get a PNG image with optional OCR

## Recommended Workflows

### Finding and Reading Documents
1. Use `remarkable_browse(query="keyword")` to search by name
2. Use `remarkable_read("Document Name")` to get content
3. Use `remarkable_read("Document", page=2)` to continue reading long documents
4. Use `remarkable_read("Document", grep="pattern")` to search within a document

### Getting Page Images
Use `remarkable_image` when you need visual context:
- Hand-drawn diagrams, sketches, or UI mockups
- Content that text extraction might miss
- Implementing designs based on hand-drawn wireframes

Example: `remarkable_image("UI Mockup", page=1)` returns a PNG image
Example: `remarkable_image("Notes", include_ocr=True)` returns image with extracted text

### For Large Documents
Use pagination to avoid overwhelming context. The response includes:
- `page` / `total_pages` - current position
- `more` - true if more content exists
- `next_page` - page number to request next

### Combining Tools
- Browse → Read: Find documents first, then read them
- Recent → Read: Check what was recently modified, then read specific ones
- Read with grep: Search for specific content within large documents
- Browse → Image: Find a document then get its visual representation

## MCP Resources

Documents are registered as resources for direct access:
- `remarkable:///{path}.txt` - Get full extracted text content in one request
- `remarkableimg:///{path}.page-{N}.png` - Get PNG image of page N (notebooks only)
- Use resources when you need complete document content without pagination… [truncated]

# SSI crosswalk: Draft v1 of the guide

Every statement in the NCAA SSI *Performance Technologies Recommendations: Responsible
Use in Collegiate Athletics* (CSMAS/SSI, March 2026), mapped to the section or appendix of
`deliverables/SSI_BestPractices_GUIDE_DRAFTv1_ER_2026-10-04` that meets it. SSI item text
is summarised from `docs/SOURCES.md` § B. Status: **Met** = the guide carries it in full;
**Met, pending** = carried, but a position in it waits on the review named in
`docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md`.

Guide sections: 0 Purpose and scope · 1 Governance · 2 Technology adoption · 3 Athlete
consent and education · 4 Data management · 5 Vendor data contracts · 6 Staff-transition
continuity · 7 Continuous improvement. Appendices: A Consent · B Vendor checklist ·
C Offboarding · D Annual review · E Technology intake.

## Foundational statements (SSI p2)

| SSI item | What SSI asks | Where the guide meets it | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 Fundamentals: broad definition | Performance technology covers devices, cameras, sensors, surveys, software and apps | §0 Definitions (SSI definition adopted verbatim in substance; scope lists video, surveys and apps) | Met |
| F1 Fundamentals: "just one tool" | Technology supports, never replaces, professional judgment | §0 Principles ("data guided, not data driven"); §4.4 interpretation rule | Met |
| F1 Fundamentals: quality varies | Assess accuracy, reliability, validity, function before selecting | §2 and Appendix E (gates and rated features) | Met |
| F2 Rights and protections | Know student-athlete rights, local and international law; watch for unintended impacts including mental health | §3 (notice vs consent, rights list), §3.5 education topics, §4.1 legal basis, §7 survey items on harm; Appendix A rights section | Met, pending (OGC: legal classification) |
| F3 Written plan | A plan for education, data management, purchase decisions and continuous improvement | The guide itself, with §1 naming owner, review and version control | Met, pending (Chris: owner and sign-off) |

## Recommendation 1: Policy

| SSI item | What SSI asks | Where the guide meets it | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rec 1 | Establish a written plan | The guide (§0–§7) plus forms A–E | Met |
| 1.1 | Multidisciplinary team, including student-athletes, develops and routinely reviews the plan | §1.1 Working Group membership (two student-athletes, Athletic Medicine, Athletic Performance, coaches, administration, OGC, ITS, Compliance); §1.3 annual review; Appendix D | Met, pending (Chris: charter the group) |
| 1.2 | Address school-specific considerations | §0 "How Baylor already works"; Baylor systems table in §4.2; tech inventory figures in §5.3; framework routing in §2 | Met |

## Recommendation 2: Education

| SSI item | What SSI asks | Where the guide meets it | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rec 2 | Routine education; foundational for informed consent | §3.5 Education, placed inside the consent section on purpose | Met |
| 2.1 | At least once a year for anyone selecting, using or accessing data | §3.5 calendar (annual staff session, orientation, preseason refresher, new-hire onboarding within 30 days); attendance tracked; Appendix D input | Met |
| 2.2 | Tailor by group | §3.5 audience table (student-athletes, coaches, Athletic Performance, Athletic Medicine, administration, ITS) | Met |
| 2.3 | Topics: limitations and harms; privacy and security; rights including consent; departmental policies | §3.5 four required topics, covered in every audience module | Met |

## Recommendation 3: Data management

| SSI item | What SSI asks | Where the guide meets it | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rec 3 | Establish ownership, storage, access and permitted use, with legal and risk management | §4.1 ownership; §4.2 storage and systems; §4.3 access matrix; §4.5 permitted and prohibited uses | Met, pending (Chris/OGC: ownership) |
| 3.1 | Who may interpret and communicate data; competencies and oversight | §4.4 interpretation competencies by data class; Data Steward role in §1.2 | Met |
| 3.2 | The school's rights over collection, use, access and ownership, including transfer athletes | §4.1 ownership position; §4.6 transfer protocol (built on the VALD records-release precedent); Appendix A | Met, pending (OGC: ownership, retention) |
| 3.3 | Permissible uses; Athletic Medicine involved in medical decisions; autonomous authority over return to play | §1.4 medical authority statement; §4.5 permitted uses; Level 3 review routes physiologic data to Athletic Medicine (§2) | Met |

## Recommendation 4: Selecting and implementing new technologies

| SSI item | What SSI asks | Where the guide meets it | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rec 4 | A structured decision process | §2 points to the Software and Technology Management Framework (three phases, two control points, three review levels) | Met, pending (Chris: framework treated as live) |
| 4.1 | Evidence-based standards for value, usability and quality | §2.2 single scoring instrument (Appendix E), built from the STRN Quality Framework and the March checklist | Met |
| 4.2 | Assess accuracy, reliability, validity and function | Appendix E rated features and decision rule; §2.3 trial and 90-day review | Met |
| 4.3 | Multidisciplinary group decides | §2.1 reviewers by level; Working Group sees every Level 2 and 3 request (§1.1) | Met |

## Recommendation 5: Continuous improvement

| SSI item | What SSI asks | Where the guide meets it | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rec 5 | Routinely get feedback and revise the plan | §7 annual cycle; Appendix D | Met |
| 5.1 | Multidisciplinary group plans, collects and interprets feedback, ideally the plan's authors | §7.1 Working Group runs the cycle; §1.3 | Met |
| 5.2 | Student-athlete feedback is critical | §7.2 annual survey, SAAC focus group, confidential concern channel, results shared back | Met |
| 5.3 | Feedback from other groups on implementation, effectiveness and education | §7.3 staff survey; technology-by-technology review tied to framework Phase 3; education effectiveness | Met |

## Where Baylor goes beyond SSI

SSI does not mention these. The guide adds them because the 9/9 SSI webinar, the tech
inventory, or Baylor's own experience made the case.

| Topic | Guide section | Why it is in |
|---|---|---|
| Vendor data contracts: ownership, exit and deletion, AI training, data-for-discount and norm pooling | §5, Appendix B | Webinar (Moderator 33:09; Koberly 34:16): purchasers and Athletic Medicine may not know a contract trades data for price. 75 of 188 inventoried products handle athlete data. No current Baylor step requires data return or deletion when a product is dropped. |
| Staff-transition continuity | §6, Appendix C | No external source covers it. Baylor's own pipelines (GPS, force plate, VALD, RTP reports) are built and run by a small number of people. |
| NIL and pay | §4.5 prohibited uses; Appendix A consent row | Webinar (Koberly 34:16): paying players raises the stakes on data use. |
| Research use | §4.5; Appendix A consent row | Only with IRB approval and separate consent; the "don't collect it if you don't use it" rule (Coffey 39:45). |
| Physiologic vs performance data classes | §4.2, §4.3 | Webinar (Koberly 34:16): physiologic data is more likely to be protected health information. |
| Algorithm transparency ("black box") | Appendix E gate; Appendix B row 12 | Webinar (Koberly 26:22, Coffey 29:10): two devices gave different scores for the same session. |

## Coverage check

24 SSI items (5 foundational, 5 recommendations, 14 strategies). 24 mapped, 0 unmapped.
